Adapter approach: reuse the sync tool the user already has (s3sync/rclone/GDrive desktop client etc.) rather than reimplementing sync — Hilo helps with install/config, or falls back to its own hilo-backends S3 engine. UX = feels like unlimited storage; multiple agents can share the same working view via the shared backend without uploading huge files. Deliverable includes a feature & compatibility matrix (backend × sync tool × modes).

reasoning:
Feature request from Bane (2026-08-26): the working space should be able to BE an S3 bucket using s3fs-like concepts (or a custom build) so the agent thinks files are local but they are really on S3 — always safe, without uploading everything. It gets its own git-ignore-style pattern ('upstream ignore') since the same pattern will be reused for S3, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc. Build artifacts and binaries don't need to be pushed up and pulled down constantly — they can stay local.
DESIGN UPDATE (Bane 08-26 follow-up): install & config help yes, but users may already have s3sync or the equivalent Google Drive client etc. — just use it. Hilo is an overlay filesystem already: it mounts itself where needed, and when the inotify engine sees files change it knows whether they are to be synced or not (ignore-aware). This gives the user what feels like unlimited storage. Google Drive and others offer keep-files-on-machine options and handle complex sync, so multiple agents that need the same working view can share it via this shared backend without uploading huge files. A feature & compatibility matrix is a required deliverable of this task. Implementation spec: specs/backend-backed-workspace-spec.md.

title: P1 — TypeScript/JS file-form impact/related is silently empty: no file→module edge resolution. Live (vite @ main, 908 files): `hilo graph impact packages/vite/src/node/server/pluginContainer.ts --max-depth 1` prints 'No dependents found' (rc 0) although edges.jsonl holds 24 incoming edges from 13 distinct importers (grep ground truth: 14 importer files). MCP vfs_graph_impact mirrors it: {"dependents":[],"total":0}, isError=false. The GAP-064 fix (9431cac, Python) and GAP-057 fix (Go) did not cover the TS/JS `local:./server/pluginContainer` target form. Only `local:<exact-specifier>` queries work, and each relative specifier (`./x` vs `../server/x`) is a separate query — a user needs N queries to see one file's dependents. FIX: resolve TS/JS file paths to their local: specifier family (or a canonical module node) inside impact/related/untested/module, mirroring the Python approach.
reasoning: Discovered in dogfood run 5 on the vite corpus: file-form impact/related answered 'structurally empty' while edges.jsonl held the real local: edges. Root cause: the JS/TS parser keeps relative specifiers verbatim as local:<spec> edge targets, so one target file is named by many nodes (one per importer-directory+specifier pair) - a per-file pkg: walk (GAP-034/057/064) cannot invert that. title: [P0] fuse: readdir on an EMPTY directory never replies -> `find`/recursive glob over the mount returns 0 rows and hangs forever
detail: dogfood run 7 (FUSE deep dive). Isolated repro on a purpose-built repo: `ls -a <mount>/emptydir` hangs to the timeout cap on EVERY attempt (rc=124/0, zero output; caps tried 8s/12s/15s/20s) while every non-empty sibling answers in ~110 ms (`. .. a.txt`). Consequence in real use: `find <mount> -type f` returned 0 rows in 3/3 runs of 15s each, against 24 rows in 111 ms on disk — so `find`, recursive globs, `git status` and any tree walk over a mount produce NOTHING and no error on any repo that contains one empty directory. Silent-empty is the worst failure shape for an agent tool. Mechanism, read from source: hilo-fuse/src/ops.rs:277 `readdir` always ends with reply.ok() EXCEPT the path at :315-321 (`files.get(&ino)` -> None => reply.error(ENOENT); return) and the case where populate_directory (:121) inserts nothing — which is exactly the empty-directory case, since its loop body runs per child. The handler returns having replied to no request, so the kernel waits forever.
reasoning: FIXED in f03a189 (P0). Reproduced first: `ls -a <mount>/emptydir` hung to a 10s cap with ZERO output (rc=124) while a non-empty sibling answered in 0.117s; `find <mount> -type f` returned 27 rows in 13.8s vs 23 on disk. Mechanism: readdir compared cookies with `<=` (offset<=1 for ".", offset<=2 for ".."), which is correct only while a later child raises the cookie past 2 — with NO children the last cookie is 2, so readdir(offset=2) re-emitted ".." with cookie 2 forever. Non-empty dirs escaped because a child cookie is >=3. Fixed by computing entries in one place with the rule "emit entry k iff offset < k" (empty batch for offset>=3, resume terminates). VERIFIED end-to-end after the fix: empty dir 10s hang -> 0.115s with `. ..`; find -type f -> 23 rows (disk ground truth) in 0.115s. 7 new tests including a kernel-replay walk asserting forward progress; the OLD logic is demonstrably red (['.', '..', '..'] then no progress). hilo_fuse 18 passed, clippy -D warnings clean.

title: [P1] fuse: `hilo mount` FAILS on a stock Debian/Ubuntu box because auto_unmount forces allow_other (user_allow_other commented out by default) and no CLI flag can turn it off
detail: dogfood run 7, on the FRESH ephemeral bunker agent (Debian 13, base image only), after a successful install leg: `hilo mount $HOME/mnt` prints 'Hilo mounted at ...' and then `fusermount3: option allow_other only allowed if 'user_allow_other' is set in /etc/fuse.conf` / `error: FUSE mount failed: Operation not permitted (os error 1)`, EXIT=1. Nobody asked for allow_other: `hilo mount --help` shows it as an opt-in flag and the generated .vfs/manifest.yaml says `allow_other: false`. Root cause traced into the dependency (fuser 0.15.1, src/mnt/mount_options.rs:26): 'AutoUnmount requires AllowOther or AllowRoot. If AutoUnmount is set and neither Allow... is set, the FUSE configuration must permit allow_other, otherwise mounting will fail.' Hilo sets auto_unmount: true (hilo-cli/src/commands/mount.rs:67) while passing allow_other: false, so the kernel refuses the mount wherever /etc/fuse.conf leaves user_allow_other commented out — the default on every Debian/Ubuntu install (verified empty on the bunker box). This is why months of local testing missed it: the dev host has user_allow_other set, so the exact same binary mounts fine there. `hilo mount --help` exposes no way to disable auto_unmount, so a stock-box user has NO CLI path to a working mount. The flagship feature of an 'agent-first virtual filesystem' is unavailable to anyone who has not first edited a root-owned config.
reasoning: FIXED in f03a189 (P1). Confirmed in source: `auto_unmount: true` was hardcoded in mount.rs while `allow_other` is opt-in, and fuser 0.15.1 requires AutoUnmount to be paired with AllowOther — so a default mount forced a privileged option the operator never chose and fusermount3 refused it on any box with user_allow_other commented out (stock Debian/Ubuntu). Fixed in mount_options(): AutoUnmount is now emitted ONLY alongside an explicit AllowOther request, since allow-other is a real access decision and outweighs a convenience flag. `auto_unmount_suppressed()` is exposed so callers can report the drop instead of silently changing behaviour. VERIFIED: a default mount (no --allow-other) now completes on this box and serves the tree — the DF-5 gate run above is itself the proof, since it mounts with no allow-other flag and reads 23 files. 3 new tests; hilo_fuse 18 passed.

title: [P1] fuse: the mount does not consult the ignore stack — `.git/`, `.vfs/` and a 130 GB `target/` are served through the mount even though `hilo ignore check target/` says ignored:true
detail: dogfood run 7. Contradiction measured on this workspace: `hilo ignore check target/` -> 'path: target ignored: true', `hilo ignore check .git/` -> 'ignored: true', `hilo ignore check target/debug/incremental` -> 'ignored: true'; yet `ls <mount>` lists target, .git, .vfs and .pytest_cache, and `ls <mount>/target` shows CACHEDIR.TAG debug release tmp. On this repo target/ is 130 GB. Mechanism: `grep -rn ignore hilo-fuse/src/*.rs` returns ZERO hits — the mount tree is built by a raw std::fs::read_dir walk (hilo-fuse/src/ops.rs:125), so ignore policy is enforced on the graph/ephemeral/backend paths but never on the mount. That also contradicts the crate's own docs (docs/hilo-fuse.md: 'mounts repositories and backends as a unified directory tree') and hilo-core/src/manifest.rs:458, which describes an 'included subtree — becomes visible to discovery' model: what ships is a raw mirror of the working directory. Impact: the mount is meant to be the zero-copy surface an agent queries; a tree containing .git/ and target/ makes every traversal both wrong (junk nodes) and enormous, and it multiplies the cost of DF-WARPFS-5's hang.
reasoning: FIXED in 3a6ef86. Confirmed the contradiction in source: `grep -rn ignore hilo-fuse/src/*.rs` returned ZERO hits — the mount tree came from a raw std::fs::read_dir walk (ops.rs:125), so ignore policy applied to the graph, ephemeral and backend paths but never to the mount. Fix: Hilo now carries an optional IgnoreMatcher; populate_directory skips excluded children BEFORE the metadata call, so an ignored 130 GB target/ is never even stat'd; `hilo mount` loads the same stack the CLI uses (built-in defaults + root .hiloignore + nested files), fail-soft on a broken file. VERIFIED end-to-end on a real mount: root now lists `. .. .gitfake a.txt src` with target/ and .git gone, `ls <mount>/target` -> No such file or directory, `src/s.rs` still served, `find -type f` -> `a.txt src/s.rs`. The CLI verdicts and the mount listing now agree. 5 new tests assert the agreement in BOTH directions, including that ordinary entries are not hidden (over-hiding is as broken as under-hiding). hilo_fuse 23 passed, clippy -D warnings clean.

title: [P2] fuse: the mount fabricates file mtimes (every file reports the time of the stat call) — mtime-based change detection is unusable through the mount
detail: dogfood run 7. Same files, disk vs mount: README.md disk 2026-09-19 20:13:55 vs mount 2026-09-19 20:47:12; Makefile disk 2026-07-19 12:15:26 vs mount 2026-09-19 20:47:12; LICENSE disk 2026-06-24 20:09:01 vs mount 2026-09-19 20:47:12. The fabricated value is not a fixed constant — it is the moment of the call: two independent mount sessions in this run reported 20:42:55 and 20:47:12 for the same unchanged files. Sizes ARE real (byte-exact vs disk) and content hashes match, so this is purely getattr metadata honesty. Mechanism: the mount's FileAttr construction never reads the backing file's metadata for time fields.
reasoning: FIXED in 09ea0fc. Confirmed in source: make_attr set atime/mtime/ctime/crtime all to SystemTime::now() — the moment of the stat call — for every inode, and never read the backing file. The fabricated value was therefore not a constant but the current time, which is why two sessions minutes apart disagreed for the same unchanged files. Fix: backing_metadata() stats the inode's real path and getattr reports atime/mtime from it (crtime via created() where available); a failed stat still falls back to now rather than erroring. VERIFIED end-to-end on a real mount with recognisable old mtimes: README.md stamped 2010-01-01 reports 2010-01-01 through the mount, Makefile stamped 2020-06-15 reports 2020-06-15, a file created now matches disk to the NANOSECOND, and two stats of an unchanged file 2s apart are byte-identical (no drift). 3 new tests: backing mtime honoured, mtime stable across calls, size still byte-exact. hilo_fuse 26 passed, hilo_graph 253 passed, clippy -D warnings clean.

title: [P0] backend: `hilo backend sync` always fails on the FIRST push to a real S3 endpoint (its own plan says 1 to transfer, then 'aws sdk error: service error') — the driver HEADs the absent remote key and only maps an error to 'not found' when the text contains the literal NotFound
detail: dogfood run 8, live S3-compatible endpoint (sourced AWS_ENDPOINT_URL/AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, bucket created, mount registered with --tool native). `hilo backend sync` -> 'plan s3data: 1 to transfer, 0 to delete, 0 skipped ignored, 0 skipped ephemeral, 0 skipped placeholders' then 'error: s3data: backend error: aws sdk error: s3: aws error: service error', EXIT=1. Same result with an explicit path arg (`hilo backend sync src`) and with --both. The endpoint's own request log shows the mechanism: 'GET /hilo-s3-dogfood/?list-type=2&prefix=dog 200' immediately followed by 'HEAD /hilo-s3-dogfood/dog/src/main.rs 404' — the driver HEADs the object it is about to upload, and S3Client::head_object_meta (hilo-backends/src/s3.rs:685-700) converts the error with `Err(e) if format!("{}", e).contains("NotFound") => Ok(None)` with a bare `Err(e) => Err(S3Error::from(e))` fallback, so a 404 whose Display does not spell 'NotFound' aborts the whole sync instead of meaning 'the remote counterpart does not exist yet -> upload'. FALSIFIABLE DISCRIMINATOR (already run): pre-create the remote key with the AWS CLI so the HEAD returns 200, then run the identical command -> 'plan s3data: 1 to transfer...' then 'synced s3data: 1 transferred (12 bytes), 1 conflicts recorded', EXIT=0. Same binary, same args; only the HEAD status differs. Impact: the single most ordinary first action of a new backend user is guaranteed to fail, while re-syncing already-present objects works — so a superficial retry-style test would pass and miss it. NOTE: `hilo workspace sync` (the other engine) handles the same fresh-bucket push correctly, which is why this survived.
reasoning: Sync stats each key before transferring it and a HEAD miss is the normal 'remote counterpart absent -> upload' state. Both HEAD helpers classified it with format!("{e}").contains("NotFound"); endpoints answering HEAD 404 with an empty body make aws-sdk deserialize Unhandled carrying only the wire code, so the Display lacks the literal and the guard missed -> Err(S3Error) -> whole sync aborted. Also over-broad the other way: any unrelated error whose text mentioned the token was swallowed as 'absent'. Fixed with one layered predicate (raw 404 status -> typed HeadObjectError::is_not_found() -> wire code NotFound) shared by head_object_meta and head_object_last_modified, with the decision core in pure fn head_failure_means_absent() so it is unit-testable without a live endpoint -- the old guard was untestable, which is why it shipped broken.

title: [P1] backend: two independent sync engines answer the same user need with different flags and different behaviour, and `backend sync` silently targets the ambient AWS endpoint (a real production bucket) when AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is unset
detail: dogfood run 8. `hilo workspace sync` (commands/workspace.rs -> SyncEngine + S3Client) and `hilo backend sync` (commands/backend.rs -> BackendRegistry/S3Driver) are both documented as the backend sync feature (README:231-233 lists `hilo backend mount` and `hilo workspace mount` side by side) but do not share a code path and disagree measurably: (a) the fresh-bucket push that fails in backend sync (see DF-WARPFS-10) SUCCEEDS in workspace sync — 2 uploaded, then a 3 MB binary verified byte-exact by sha256; (b) --pull/--push/--both exist only on backend sync (workspace sync rejects them: 'error: unexpected argument --pull found', EXIT=2, while its own default is two-way); (c) backend sync refuses to run without a registered mount ('No backends configured in manifest.') while workspace sync needs no mount; (d) THE SHARP ONE — with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL UNSET, `hilo backend sync` planned against the REAL cloud endpoint configured in the operator's ambient ~/.aws/config ('plan s3data: 1 to transfer', then failure), because S3Client::new (hilo-backends/src/s3.rs:99-118) only builds an explicit endpoint client when AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is present and otherwise takes aws_config::defaults(BehaviorVersion::latest()).load() (the ambient chain). The CLI never states which store it resolved, so the same command means 'local test server' or 'my production bucket' depending on an env var, revealed only as a count in a plan line. Impact: a user cannot tell from the CLI which endpoint a two-way sync is about to write to — for a tool whose whole promise is that remote state is safe to sync.
reasoning: Two fixes, in priority order. (1) SAFETY/DISCLOSURE: every backend/sync command must print the resolved endpoint (and bucket/region) in its plan line, so 'which store am I writing to' is never a guess; a `--endpoint` flag or explicit config field is preferable to an env-only switch for a destructive path. (2) CONSOLIDATION: converge on one engine (or at minimum one flag vocabulary) — today the working implementation and the documented one are different programs, and the README presents them as one feature. PASS: `hilo backend sync` (and workspace sync) prints the resolved endpoint URL and bucket in the plan header, and a test pins that the printed endpoint equals the one the client was constructed with; plus a decision recorded for the two-engine split (either the flags are unified or the docs name which command is canonical).

title: [P1] tests: the S3 integration suite reports `7 passed` without exercising a single line of S3 — the readiness gate demands MinIO's own health path and a non-MinIO endpoint is reported as a PASS, so it is phantom coverage for exactly the surface DF-WARPFS-10 breaks
detail: dogfood run 8. Measured twice on the same tree. (a) No endpoint configured: `cargo test -p hilo_backends --test s3_integration_test` -> 'running 7 tests' / 'test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured' finished in 0.23s. (b) With a LIVE S3-compatible server answering on AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:19001 (moto, bucket created, AWS CLI verified objects in it): the identical run -> 'test result: ok. 7 passed' finished in 0.05s — 50ms for seven tests that claim to put/get/list/head/delete against real S3 infrastructure. Mechanism: every test body starts with `let endpoint = require_minio!();` whose check_minio_available() (hilo-backends/tests/s3_integration_test.rs:32-57) builds '{endpoint}/minio/health/live' and requires HTTP 200 from curl; moto answers 404 there (200 on '/'), so the macro hits `eprintln!("SKIP: ..."); return;` — and a returned test is counted as passed. The file header documents the skip as deliberate ('Tests are skipped gracefully (return early and pass) when AWS_ENDPOINT_URL is not set OR when the endpoint is not reachable, so cargo test never fails on machines without Docker/MinIO running'), so the intent is honest; the defect is that a skip is indistinguishable from a pass in the report AND the readiness probe tests 'is this MinIO' rather than 'can I reach an S3 endpoint'. Impact: this file is the only coverage signal for the S3 backend, and it is green in every environment that is not exactly MinIO — including CI — which is why DF-WARPFS-10 (first push to a fresh bucket always fails) could ship. Same class as the INT-GITREINS-002/003 pattern this repo already documented for the rust-analyzer/LSP legs.
reasoning: Three changes make this honest and useful. (1) The probe must test the protocol, not the vendor: probe with a real S3 call (HeadBucket/ListObjectsV2 against the configured endpoint+creds) and accept any endpoint that answers, instead of a hard-coded /minio/health/live path. (2) A skip must be visible as a skip: `#[ignore]` with an explicit env-gated runner, or a hard failure when AWS_ENDPOINT_URL IS set but the endpoint is unusable — never a bare `return` that the harness scores as ok. (3) Add the missing case that would have caught DF-WARPFS-10: plan-and-upload to an EMPTY bucket via the backend/sync driver path (not only the S3Client primitive path). PASS: with AWS_ENDPOINT_URL set to a live non-MinIO S3 endpoint, the suite either runs its assertions for real (and would FAIL against the current head/NotFound defect) or reports an explicit skip count > 0; it must not report '7 passed' in 0.05s. Prove it by re-running the suite by hand against a fresh endpoint both ways.

title: [P1] ffi: every hilo-ffi graph function resolves `.vfs/graph/graph.db` from the EMBEDDING PROCESS's CWD and vfs_graph_related's `path` argument is never used for resolution — a host application gets a confident empty graph indistinguishable from 'no dependencies'
detail: dogfood run 8, first run to consume hilo-ffi. The crate builds clean (cargo build -p hilo_ffi RC=0, 16m06s) and really exports the UniFFI ABI for Go/Python/Kotlin/Swift (`nm -D --defined-only target/debug/libhilo_ffi.so` -> uniffi_hilo_ffi_fn_func_vfs_{get_metadata,set_metadata,graph_related,graph_impact,graph_stats,list_directory,resolve_backend,rule_check} + checksums + UNIFFI_META_UDL_HILO) — the library half is honest. The resolution half is not: hilo-ffi/src/lib.rs vfs_graph_related/vfs_graph_impact/vfs_graph_stats/vfs_rule_check all hard-code `let db_path = ".vfs/graph/graph.db";` and `if !std::path::Path::new(db_path).exists() { return Ok(<empty>); }`, and vfs_graph_related(path) passes `path` straight to db.related(...) while LOOKING UP the database by the literal relative path — so the argument that identifies the subject never participates in finding the graph. vfs_rule_check likewise probes 'manifest.yaml' then '.vfs/manifest.yaml' (same shape, and note the primary/fallback order differs from the CLI's fallback set). The CLI has the same CWD-relative architecture but the CLI is documented as a per-repo tool run inside the repo; an FFI consumer is by definition a host program (a Python service, a Swift app, a Go binary) whose CWD is its own. Verified consequence exists on every other surface in this project's history: when resolution silently misses, the answer is an empty list that reads exactly like a true empty — the failure mode GAP-039/GAP-059/GAP-062 had to be fixed for on the CLI and MCP surfaces. Plus one observable mismatch: vfs_list_directory returns absolute paths, while the graph functions key off relative-to-CWD paths, so the directory the consumer just listed is not necessarily the directory the graph is read from.
reasoning: An embedding API cannot depend on the host's working directory. FIX DIRECTION: give the FFI an explicit root — a `HiloHandle`/config object constructed with a repo root path (the natural UniFFI shape), or at minimum an env/`set_root` entry point — and resolve the graph and manifest against it; when the root is unset or the graph is missing, return a DISTINCT error (HiloError::NotFound/InternalError with the resolved path in the message) instead of an empty result. The `path` argument of vfs_graph_related should be resolved against the same root. PASS: from a process whose CWD is / (or any unrelated directory), a consumer can still obtain real graph stats/related/impact for a repo it names explicitly, and a missing graph yields an error naming the resolved path rather than a zeros/empty payload; a test drives the FFI from a deliberately foreign CWD.

title: [P1] ffi+mcp: vfs_resolve_backend / vfs_backend_status / vfs_sync_backend / vfs_resolve_path return hardcoded constants (`backend:"local"`, `last_synced:"synced"`, `synced_files:1`) — measured over MCP with a real S3 backend mounted they still said 'local'/'synced'
detail: dogfood run 8. hilo-ffi/src/lib.rs vfs_resolve_backend(path) is: `let exists = p.exists(); Ok(BackendInfo { path, backend: Some("local".to_string()), remote_url: None, cache_path: None, last_synced: if exists { Some("synced".to_string()) } else { None }, cached: Some(exists) })` — i.e. the backend identity is a literal and 'last synced' is the word 'synced' meaning nothing more than 'the path exists on disk'. The MCP twins are the same shape (hilo-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:922-1005): vfs_resolve_path returns backend:"local"/sync_status:"synced" when the file exists, vfs_backend_status returns {backend:"local", cache_hit, cache_path, remote_url, last_synced}, and vfs_sync_backend carries the comment 'For local backends, returns synced_files = 1 (always in sync)'. MEASURED live over a real stdio MCP session (initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call) in a workspace where an S3 backend WAS mounted (mounts.yaml present, entry for s3://hilo-s3-dogfood/dog/ at /s3data): vfs_backend_status {path:src/main.rs} -> {"backend":"local","cache_hit":true,"cache_path":null,"last_synced":"synced","remote_url":null}; vfs_sync_backend {path:src/main.rs} -> {"errors":[],"skipped_ignored":0,"synced_files":1}; vfs_resolve_path {path:src/main.rs} -> {"backend":"local","cached":true,"real_path":"/tmp/dogfood-warpfs-mount/src/main.rs","sync_status":"synced"}. Impact: an agent asking the two questions this surface exists for — 'where does this file actually come from?' and 'is my remote copy current?' — is answered by constants that are wrong the moment a backend is real. Combined with DF-WARPFS-11 (backend list is blind) the entire backend surface can no longer report a real backend anywhere a program can read it. Note the MCP surface is where this is most damaging, because MCP is the agent-facing path and an agent has no way to notice the answer is canned.
reasoning: Returning a constant where a fact is expected is worse than returning an error, because it is indistinguishable from good news. FIX DIRECTION: resolve the path against the manifest/mounts.yaml (the same source the mount path writes) and report the real backend kind, remote/bucket, cache path and last-sync timestamp; when no backend governs the path, say so (a distinct 'unmanaged'/'local-only' value with the resolved origin) rather than defaulting to 'local'+'synced'. FIX `vfs_sync_backend` to actually drive a sync (or return a not-supported error) instead of reporting synced_files=1 unconditionally. PASS: with an S3 mount registered in mounts.yaml, vfs_backend_status/vfs_resolve_path report backend 's3' with the real bucket/prefix from that entry, and vfs_sync_backend either performs the sync or errors; a test asserts the reported backend changes when the mount config changes.

detail: dogfood run 8. title: [P1] tests: a flaky `hilo_graph` lib test blocks the GitReins Tier-1 commit guard — `cargo test -p hilo_graph --lib` failed on an unchanged tree (semantic.rs:785 NotFound) while a dogfood commit was being made, then passed on 9/9 subsequent runs
detail: dogfood run 8. While committing docs/board-only changes (no .rs touched: `git status --short hilo-graph/` empty), `gitreins commit -F <msg>` was BLOCKED by Tier 1: 'Tier 1 Guards: FAIL (test mode: full)' / 'tests (full) - error: test failed, to rerun pass -p hilo_graph --lib', with the guard log showing 'test result: FAILED. 252 passed; 1 failed' and '---- semantic::tests::search_with_symbols_finds_defining_file_by_exact_symbol stdout ---- thread ... panicked at hilo-graph/src/semantic.rs:785:45: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: "No such file or directory" }'. Line 785 is the test's `std::env::set_current_dir(prev_cwd).unwrap()` — the RESTORE call, so the failure is not the search assertion but the CWD restore itself. Mechanism (source read, not speculation): this test and its sibling `search_without_symbols_keeps_path_only_behavior` both do `std::env::set_current_dir(dir.path())` / restore `prev_cwd` (semantic.rs:779/785/799/802), while `std::env::set_current_dir` is PROCESS-GLOBAL and the default cargo test harness runs tests on parallel threads. Every other test in the binary that touches a relative path (many resolve the literal '.vfs/graph/graph.db' or './...') therefore runs with a CWD that a concurrent thread may have redirected into a `TempDir`, and the `TempDir` can be dropped by its owner mid-run — which is exactly an ENOENT on a relative path. Honest evidence limits: observed ONCE, under heavy concurrent load (this host runs 3 other builds simultaneously; loadavg 23-29). Not reproduced afterwards in 9 runs — the test alone (1 pass), the two CWD-mutating tests filtered together x5 (25 passed each), and the full lib suite x3 (253 passed each). So the flake rate is low but the impact is high: the guard is fail-closed, so ANY occurrence blocks every commit in the repo until it goes green again, and it blocked a docs-only commit. Also note the correct-reasoning trap: the same CWD-relative architecture is not itself a bug for the CLI (documented per-repo), but it IS a hazard inside the test binary where tests share one process.
reasoning: FIX DIRECTION: stop mutating process-global state in tests. Prefer passing the root explicitly to `search(...)`/the resolver (a root/cwd parameter or a config struct) and have the two tests pass the TempDir path; if a signature change is too wide, serialize the CWD-mutating tests with a shared mutex (`static CWD_LOCK: Mutex<()>` taken by every test that reads a relative path or calls set_current_dir — `serial_test` is the off-the-shelf form) so the suite is deterministic under any scheduling. Either way the suite must not depend on the CWD of a sibling thread. PASS: the full `cargo test -p hilo_graph --lib` suite passes under a concurrently loaded host (re-run x10 while a workspace build runs) with no intervention, AND a deliberate RED proof exists: with the CWD held in another directory, the test still finds its file. Related: this is the same load-sensitivity class as GAP-089 (bound test-suite host load) — worth checking whether the fleet's parallel builds are what exposed it.

title: P0 - DuckDB cache reconcile costs ~145 KB of RAM PER EDGE: replaying edges.jsonl into graph.db peaks at 2.9 GB for 20K edges (linear, ~0.14 MB/edge) and ~21.6 GB for grafana's 155K edges - while the same query on a warm cache uses 53 MB. memory_limit/threads are also declared in the manifest and never applied.
detail: hilo-vs-scc bake-off wave 6 (2026-09-20), hilo @ 89d44fb (binary ~/bakeoff-scc-hilo/hilo-w6-bin). Measured with /usr/bin/time -f %M on synthetic corpora sampled from the grafana edges.jsonl, fresh dir per N (cold = graph.db absent, so GraphDB::open takes the reconcile replay path): N=5,000 -> 829 MB peak / 34.7 s; N=10,000 -> 1,446 MB / 37.3 s; N=20,000 -> 2,945 MB / 96.7 s. Least squares: peak_KB = 145.75*N + 81,348, i.e. ~0.142 MB per edge, base ~79 MB. That fit predicts 21.6 GB for grafana's 155,395 edges; the observed cold grafana run peaked at 18.8 GB (VmHWM 18,791,988 kB) and was still climbing at 18.4 GB after 23 min before being killed. CONTROL (same corpus, same binary, same sandbox): re-running `graph stats` on the already-reconciled 20K corpus peaked at 54,160 kB (52.9 MB) in 0.10 s - a 56x memory and ~970x time difference, isolating the entire cost to the reconcile INSERT path. During the blowup the on-disk graph.db stayed at 12,288 bytes while RSS was 14.1 GB, i.e. rows are buffered mid-transaction, not written. Mechanism: hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:288 reconcile_edges_from_jsonl opens ONE transaction (conn.execute_batch('BEGIN TRANSACTION')) and issues a prepared INSERT OR IGNORE per row against a table carrying CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_edges_unique (from,to,rel,provenance) (graph.rs:153-159). A single 155K-row open transaction must retain the entire index/payload delta in memory before COMMIT; nothing commits incrementally and there is no progress bound.
reasoning: REVISED 2026-09-20 after deeper measurement - the first version of this row was WRONG in one respect and this row supersedes it. It originally read as a sizing/knob bug and claimed a cold rebuild under a 6 GB cap succeeded. That success was invalid: it was a warm-cached run that never executed the replay (the run printed 'all cached, graph unchanged'). Reproduced properly, this is a hard, linear, unbounded memory blowup on the insert path - a P0 resource bug, not a tuning preference. ROOT CAUSE 1 (the blowup): reconcile replays every edge inside a SINGLE BEGIN/COMMIT (graph.rs:288-345), so peak memory tracks the whole corpus delta rather than a bounded batch. FIX: chunk the replay (e.g. 5-10K rows per transaction, COMMIT between chunks) and/or use DuckDB bulk ingest (COPY/Appender) instead of per-row prepared INSERT, so peak memory is bounded by chunk size, not N. Also consider SET preserve_insertion_order=false and a real SET threads for the load. ROOT CAUSE 2 (dead knobs, still true): hilo-core/src/manifest.rs:856 declares performance.duckdb.memory_limit (default 512MB, manifest.rs:124-126) and manifest.rs:853-854 declares duckdb.threads - grep shows NEITHER is ever consumed. The only live manifest.performance reader is hilo-cli/src/commands/serve.rs:65 (rate_limit_rps). The connection is opened bare: hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:369 Connection::open(path), with no SET memory_limit / SET threads / duckdb Config. So the documented knobs are dead config and DuckDB's own default applies (80% of the cgroup/host limit), which is why the failure surfaces as a raw duckdb Out of Memory error with a SET memory_limit hint the user cannot act on through hilo's own config. FIX: apply both settings when opening the graph connection and validate them. PASS criteria: (a) a test proves the configured memory_limit is actually applied to the connection; (b) a cold reconcile of a 155K-edge corpus completes within the configured limit, peak RSS bounded by chunk size and roughly flat as N grows (measure with /usr/bin/time %M); (c) warm-vs-cold memory ratio collapses from ~56x toward parity. Do not regress correctness: the corrupted-cache repair story (GAP-018/GAP-026, read-through reconciliation) must still rebuild a missing graph.db from edges.jsonl. EVIDENCE + snapshots: ~/bakeoff-scc-hilo/wave6-memleak/ (ps/status/smaps_rollup/arena analysis, repro_snapshot.txt, scaling_probe.sh) and /tmp/scale_test/ (per-N corpora + time logs). Board pre-image: /tmp/tasks.jsonl.pre-gap092-fix. RELATED ROW: GAP-093 (P1, bane-direct-2026-09-20) is the umbrella SAFETY row for the same observation - it records the symptom (no memory ceiling: 17.9 GB peak / 3.2 GB swap against a declared 512 MB) and points here for the root cause. Fix them together: GAP-092 owns the mechanism + the scaling law + the chunked-replay fix; GAP-093 owns the 'the tool must not grow until the host dies' acceptance surface. Neither is a duplicate of the other.

title: P1 — the running application has NO memory ceiling: `hilo graph stats` on grafana (23,395 files) measured 17.9 GB peak RSS / 3.2 GB SWAP against its own manifest declaring 512 MB, because the only knob it ships is dead config (GAP-092) — so the tool grows until the HOST runs out, not until HILO does
reasoning:
Measured live 2026-09-20 on this host (16-core shared agent box, 61 GB RAM / 56 GB swap), Bane-requested follow-up to the bake-off wave-5 finding. Process: `/home/kara/bakeoff-scc-hilo/hilo-w6-bin graph stats`, cwd /tmp/bakeoff5/grafana, corpus 23,395 files / 2.6 GB.

MEASURED (read straight from /proc/<pid>/status, three samples over ~25 min):
  VmHWM  = 18,791,988 kB (17.9 GB peak)
  VmRSS  = 16,184,812 -> 16,845,808 kB (still CLIMBING ~50 MB / 8 s at the last sample)
  VmSwap = 3,342,856 kB (3.2 GB swapped out)
  VmPeak = 22,795,464 kB (21.7 GB address space)
  Threads = 16, CPU = 173% (1.7 cores)
  Declared by the project's OWN manifest (.vfs/manifest.yaml, written by `hilo init`): performance.duckdb.memory_limit: 512MB, threads: 4.
  Peak / declared = 35.8x. RSS / declared = 32.1x.

The run never produced a graph: `.vfs/graph/graph.db` stayed at 12,288 bytes for the whole run (WAL 1,071 bytes) while edges.jsonl is 26,057,171 bytes / ~155k edges. So the 18 GB is consumed and the deliverable is not produced — it is not 'memory well spent'.

WHY THERE IS NO CEILING (source read, warpfs @ 6006cdc):
  1. The ceiling the tool ships is dead. `performance.duckdb.memory_limit` is declared at hilo-core/src/manifest.rs:856 (default_duckdb_memory() = "512MB", manifest.rs:124-126) and GREP-CONFIRMED to have NO live consumer anywhere: the only hits are the declaration, the default fn and the tests. `GraphDB` opens the connection bare at hilo-graph/src/graph.rs (`Connection::open(path)`) with no `SET memory_limit` / PRAGMA / duckdb Config, so DuckDB falls back to its OWN default (a fraction of physical RAM, i.e. tens of GB here). This is row GAP-092 and it is the load-bearing half of this one: a declared 512 MB limit that is never applied is indistinguishable from no limit at all.
  2. `stats()` runs four unbounded aggregates over the whole edge table (hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:966-1040): two `COUNT(DISTINCT ...)` plus the orphan anti-join `WHERE e."from" NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT "to" FROM edges)` (graph.rs:1021). A NOT IN against a DISTINCT subquery materialises the full distinct-node set; nothing is streamed, nothing is paged, and the result set is built in memory before printing.
  3. `GraphDB::open` replays the whole edges.jsonl through a prepared statement inside one transaction whenever the fingerprint stamp misses (graph.rs:288-320, reconcile_needed at graph.rs:263). 26 MB of JSONL is parsed into 155k Edge structs in one transaction — fine on its own, unbounded in combination with (1).

Honest limits of this evidence: the process had already exited by the time I went to read its exit code, so I did NOT capture rc, and it was not an OOM-kill (no kernel OOM line, and the host's available memory returned to 42 GB immediately). The 3.2 GB of swap shows the host, not the process, was absorbing the bill — on a 16 GB box this exact command is an OOM, and the earlier in-sandbox OOMs Bane hit were the same curve truncated at 4 GB. I did not re-run it under a ulimit to capture a bounded reproduction; the discriminator below covers that.

WHY IT MATTERS: `graph stats` is the FIRST command a new user runs after `hilo init`, and on any realistically-sized repo it is an unbounded allocation with no warning, no progress, no ceiling and no failure message the user can act on. For a tool that advertises a 512 MB default it is a trust bug, not just a perf bug.

reasoning:
Bane-requested follow-up (2026-09-20) to the bake-off wave-5 finding: GAP-093 covers the ONE-SHOT CLI (`hilo graph stats` grows to 17.9 GB then exits). This row covers the process that DOESN'T exit — the MCP server an agent leaves running for hours, and by extension the FUSE mount with --triggers.

MECHANISM. Every MCP tool call does `hilo_graph::GraphDB::open(GRAPH_DB_PATH)` — 8 call sites in hilo-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs (L495,569,589,624,651,696,737,841). `GraphDB::open` (hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:367) calls `reconcile_needed()` (graph.rs:263), a fingerprint gate against `.vfs/graph/.last_reconcile`. On a fingerprint MISS it runs `reconcile_edges_from_jsonl()` (graph.rs:288) — the FULL edges.jsonl replay — INSIDE the request path, in the already-resident process (graph.rs:302 `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, per-row prepared `INSERT OR IGNORE`).

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN GAP-093. The one-shot CLI pays the replay once and exits, so the kernel reclaims everything and any OOM kill is contained. A resident server pays it ON TOP OF live state, cannot be reclaimed, and has NO timeout on the replay: one tool call simply blocks (207.2s measured here) while RSS climbs. On grafana (155k edges, ~21.6 GB replay predicted by GAP-092's law) that is a host-killer, and the three failure modes are silent — the client sees only a slow call, not a reason.

Also: the manifest's memory_limit/threads are dead config (GAP-092), so there is no ceiling to hit. Warm-path is genuinely flat (40.9 -> 43.3 MB over 40 calls, fds constant) — this is NOT a leak, and should not be fixed as one.

FIX DIRECTION. (a) bound the replay: stream/batch new rows so peak is independent of corpus size (shared with GAP-092); (b) apply the manifest's memory_limit/threads for real; (c) never do a full reconcile on a read-only query path — if the fingerprint misses because another writer appended, ingest only the DELTA, or serve the query against the cache and reconcile out-of-band; (d) surface the replay's progress/timeout to the client instead of blocking silently.

ACCEPTANCE. A resident server that has answered a warm-path call must NEVER run an unbounded full replay inside a request: add a test asserting peak RSS stays within N x warm baseline across a mid-session edges.jsonl change, and that no single tool call exceeds a bounded wall-clock. Both must fail on the current binary.

RELATED: GAP-092 (the per-new-row cost law + dead memory_limit/threads), GAP-093 (one-shot CLI ceiling). This row shares 092's fix but is a distinct surface — do not close 092 by fixing only the CLI.

reasoning:
Bane-directed follow-up (2026-09-20). This is the RESOLUTION SHAPE for the ceiling GAP-093 demands: 093 says the application must have a ceiling; this row says what it must DO when it reaches one.

TODAY there is no behaviour at a ceiling because there is no ceiling: `manifest.rs:856 memory_limit` (default 512MB) is declared and never consumed, `threads` likewise, and `graph.rs:369` opens the connection bare with no SET/PRAGMA. Measured consequence: ~146 KB of RAM per NEW edge (GAP-092), 2.9 GB at 20K edges and ~21.6 GB predicted / 18.8 GB observed on a 155K-edge corpus. The process does not stop at its budget, it stops when the HOST runs out.

THE DIRECTIVE is an adaptive degrade-to-disk policy with JSONL as the spill/serve medium. That choice is architecturally correct here rather than arbitrary: edges.jsonl is already the canonical, append-only, streamable source of truth, with DuckDB explicitly documented as a REBUILDABLE CACHE that is NOT the source of truth. Spilling to JSONL therefore degrades the cache back to its own source instead of inventing a new durability format - and the file is already present in every project, so there is nothing to migrate.

INTERACTION WITH THE OTHER ROWS - do not solve these independently:
- GAP-092 owns the per-new-row cost law; its chunked-commit fix IS rung 2 of this ladder. Land them together.
- GAP-093 owns 'there must be an enforced ceiling'; this row owns the behaviour AT the ceiling. Wiring memory_limit without a spill policy just converts an OOM into a hard error.
- GAP-094 owns the resident-process surface; rung 3 must be reachable from a long-lived server, otherwise the daemon still allocates unbounded on a mid-session change.

NON-NEGOTIABLE: correctness of results must not silently change with the mode. A degraded answer must be LABELLED degraded, and the streaming path must return the same edge set the DuckDB path would - otherwise the stability fix becomes a quiet correctness bug.

reasoning:
Bane directive 2026-09-21: 'use cargo flamegraph, time -p/hyperfine, SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN / dbstat, custom SVG parsing, Samply, Criterion, cargo-instruments, and tokio-console to identify speedups.' This row is the directed sweep. Three of the eight tools are already available, three needed installing and TWO DO NOT APPLY AS WRITTEN — the corrections are the point of the row, because following the list literally would have sent someone hunting for a SQLite query planner in a codebase that has no SQLite in it.

=== TOOL MATRIX (verified against this host + this workspace, 2026-09-21) ===

ALREADY PRESENT:
  - `time -p`          POSIX, always available. Coarse; use only for a first-order read.
  - `hyperfine`        1.20.0 present. Correct tool for CLI-level A/B (warmup + N runs + statistics). Prefer over `time` for anything you intend to quote as a number.
  - `perf`             7.0.14 present. `perf stat` for counters, `perf record` for stacks.
  - Criterion          ALREADY WIRED: hilo-graph has criterion 0.5 with html_reports as a dev-dependency and THREE benches already exist (benches/graph_bench.rs, semantic_bench.rs, signal_bench.rs; harness=false). hilo-fuse also carries criterion. So this is 'run and extend', NOT 'add Criterion'. Missing: a Criterion bench for the reconcile/insert path and for stats().

INSTALLED FOR THIS SWEEP (was absent):
  - `cargo flamegraph` (flamegraph crate) — wraps perf; emits the folded stacks.
  - `samply`           — sampling profiler + Firefox-Profiler UI; the better fit than cargo-flamegraph when the SVG is too large to read as text.
  - `tokio-console`    — async task/await introspection.
  - `cargo criterion`  — bench runner that keeps Criterion's history between runs.

CORRECTION 1 — SQLite EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN / DBSTAT: THE ENGINE IS DuckDB.
  Verified: the workspace links `duckdb = { version = "1.1", features = ["bundled"] }` in hilo-graph, hilo-cli and hilo-triggers. `grep -rn rusqlite --include=Cargo.toml .` returns NOTHING. There is no SQLite in this project, so `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` and `dbstat` have no target as written. The DuckDB equivalents:
     total time         -> `EXPLAIN ANALYZE <query>` (gives the operator tree + TIMING)
     plan only          -> `EXPLAIN <query>`
     storage/page stats -> `PRAGMA database_size` and the `duckdb_*` / `pragma_*` table functions (dbstat's page-level analogue: `PRAGMA database_size` for the file view, `duckdb_memory()` for the allocator view, `duckdb_temporary_files()` for spill)
     per-operator cost  -> the `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` tree, plus `SET enable_profiling='json'` if a machine-readable profile is wanted
  The highest-value query-plan target is already named in GAP-093: `stats()` runs four full-table aggregates including `WHERE e."from" NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT "to" FROM edges)` (hilo-graph/src/graph.rs:1021) — a NOT IN over a DISTINCT subquery is exactly the shape that a plan tree exposes as a materialisation + anti-join, and rewriting it as a LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL or an anti-join on a hash table is the classic fix. Measure the plan BEFORE proposing the rewrite.

CORRECTION 2 — cargo-instruments is macOS-only (it drives Xcode Instruments). This host is x86_64 Linux (AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS). It cannot run here and must not be added to any gate or checklist. Linux equivalent for that slot: perf + samply (already installed) — samply's Firefox-Profiler view is the closest thing to Instruments' timeline here.

LIMITED-APPLICABILITY FLAG — tokio-console: hilo does use tokio, but NOT as a long-lived async server in the hot path. The only runtime construction sites are hilo-cli/src/commands/workspace.rs:104 and mount.rs:245, both `Builder::new_current_thread()`. A current-thread runtime has minimal task-scheduling surface to introspect. tokio-console also requires the app to opt in (console-subscriber + a tokio_unstable build), which is a code change, not just a tool install. So: LOW expected yield against the graph hot paths; do NOT add console-subscriber to the workspace on this row's authority. If it is tried, scope it to hilo-fuse (tokio 'full') and treat it as an experiment.

=== ENVIRONMENT BLOCKER FOUND AND CLEARED ===
  kernel.perf_event_paranoid was 4 (this kernel's most restrictive setting) — perf and every perf-backed tool (cargo-flamegraph, samply) were ROOT-ONLY, which is why no profile has ever been taken on this box. It is NOW 1 (CPU event access allowed), verified: `perf stat -e cycles,instructions true` exits 0 and reports real counters as the non-root user.
  OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED: the change is RUNTIME-ONLY (`sysctl -w`) and reverts on reboot. Persisting it means adding `kernel.perf_event_paranoid = 1` to /etc/sysctl.conf, which is a host-wide security-posture change and is deliberately NOT made here. Decide deliberately; do not let a profiling row quietly loosen a host setting forever.

=== CUSTOM SVG PARSING — ALREADY BUILT AND PROVEN (this half is DONE) ===
  Built ~/.hermes/scripts/fgparse.py: reads a flamegraph SVG as TEXT and ranks frames by total or SELF time, because this agent cannot view images and the SVG carries the whole call tree. Verification is a known-answer fixture, not 'it ran': /tmp/fg_known.svg encodes a tree whose self-times are known by hand (next_token 450, read 400, build 100, helper 50, interior nodes 0) and the parser is machine-checked against all nine values — ALL CORRECT. It unescapes `operator<<` and exits 2 (not 0) on an SVG with no call tree, so 'no profile' can never be mistaken for 'nothing is hot'.
  WORTH RECORDING: the FIRST version of that parser was wrong. A parent frame is written BARE inside its children's titles (`all;parse (600 samples, 45.0%)`) while its own title carries the annotation (`all (1000 samples, 100.0%)`). Comparing stacks without normalising every segment made every self-time silently equal its total time — a plausible-looking table that was pure fiction. The known-answer fixture is what caught it. Keep that fixture when the parser is touched.

=== WORK ORDER (measure first; no fix is proposed on this row) ===
  1. hyperfine a CLI baseline: cold `graph warm`, warm `graph warm`, `graph stats`, `graph impact`, `backend sync` — on a FIXED corpus checked into /tmp, with --warmup. Publish the numbers.
  2. `perf record` + flamegraph (and samply for a second view) each of those, then run `python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/fgparse.py <svg> --self --top 40` and paste the ranked table into the row. The flame leaf that dominates is the answer.
  3. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` the `stats()` aggregates and the reconcile INSERT (the GAP-092 path, now chunked at RECONCILE_CHUNK_ROWS=2048 — verify chunking did not cost more in TOTAL time than it saved in peak memory; that is a real risk of the very fix that closed GAP-092).
  4. Backfill Criterion benches for reconcile/insert and stats() so the next regression is caught by a number rather than a flamegraph.
  5. THEN file targeted speedup rows from what the measurements show. Not before.

BUILD LOCATION (AGENTS.md policy): heavy builds belong on bunker-las-03 (6-core i5-8500T). PROFILING is the documented exception — it needs the local binary against local corpora, so profiling runs HERE on the Ryzen 7840HS (also the more representative machine).

PASS: (a) a ranked flamegraph table from fgparse for at least 'graph warm' and 'graph stats' on a fixed corpus, with the dominating leaf NAMED; (b) hyperfine numbers for those commands with the corpus and run count stated; (c) an EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the stats() aggregates showing whether the NOT IN anti-join materialises; (d) a statement of what chunking did to total cold reconcile time. No speedup claim without the measurement that produced it.

CORRECTION TO GAP-093 — one of its two root-cause claims does not survive measurement, and it is recorded here rather than quietly dropped. GAP-093 asserted that `stats()` 'nothing is streamed, nothing is paged, and the result set is built in memory' and that the orphan query's `NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT "to" FROM edges)` 'materialises the full distinct-node set'. MEASURED: DuckDB's optimiser rewrites that NOT IN into `HASH_JOIN -> MARK` — a hash anti-join, which is the efficient form, not a materialisation. None of the six stats() queries contains MATERIALIZE or NESTED_LOOP_JOIN, and the entire set completes in 11.4 ms at 26,134 edges (slowest single query 3.8 ms). So the aggregates were NEVER the memory hog, and the anti-join was never the defect. The real cause of GAP-093's 17.9 GB was the ingest path — the SAME bug already filed and fixed as GAP-092 (edge inserts, ~0.14 MB/edge, now chunked at RECONCILE_CHUNK_ROWS=2048). GAP-093's /proc measurement reproduced GAP-092's pre-fix baseline (18.8 GB) rather than discovering a new cause; its window was replayed to the same number as GAP-092's 155K figure. GAP-093's remaining unique value is the OBSERVABILITY half (no ceiling, no progress, no user-visible failure) and the `graph stats` context, both of which landed (22bf4fd).

LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a source-read hypothesis about a query planner is not a measurement. `EXPLAIN` costs one command and would have caught this before the row was filed. Run the plan FIRST for any claim of the form 'this query materialises / doesn't stream / is O(N^2)'. The same discipline that GAP-092's author applied (measure the baseline, don't infer it) applies to the SECOND-order claim about how the engine executes a query.

REDIRECT FOR THE SWEEP, from this measurement: the SQL layer is not where the speedups are (11.4 ms total). Spend the profiling budget on the INGEST/PARSE path (tree-sitter parse + edges.jsonl replay — the path GAP-092 chunked, which needs its total-time cost checked) and on process-level work (cold start, DuckDB open/attach, per-key S3 HEAD fan-out). A flamegraph of `graph warm` and `backend sync` will be far more informative than one of `graph stats`.

PROFILE RESULTS (2026-09-21) — first real measurements. All three tools exercised end-to-end: hyperfine -> perf record -> flamegraph SVG -> fgparse (custom SVG parsing) -> ranked text table. n=420 perf samples on a 2000-file corpus.

FINDING A (methodological, blocks everything else): 55.4% OF THE PROFILE IS `[unknown]`. Cargo.toml has NO `[profile.release]` section at all, and the release binary carries ZERO `.debug_` sections (readelf), so more than half of all samples cannot be attributed to a function. Every speedup judgement made from the current profile is being made on ~45% of the data. CHEAP FIX, worth doing before any optimisation work: add `[profile.release] debug = 1` (or `debug = "line-tables-only"`) and `strip = "none"` to the workspace Cargo.toml. This costs binary size, NOT runtime; the shipped artefact can still be stripped later. NOTE this is not a claim that the profile is useless — the symbolized 45% is perfectly actionable — it is a claim that the remaining 55% is currently unpriced, and it may contain the real hot leaf.

FINDING B (the hottest symbolized CLUSTER — substring searching, ~36% of symbolized self-time): `<StrSearcher>::new` 10.6% SELF, `<&str as Pattern>::is_contained_in` 12.6%, `core::slice::memchr::memchr_aligned` 12.8%, `<str>::trim_start_matches::<char>::is_whitespace` 5.8%. The load-bearing one is `StrSearcher::new` at 10.6% SELF: constructing the searcher is itself a top-6 cost, which means a substring pattern is being COMPILED repeatedly instead of once. The standard fix is a precompiled finder — `memchr::memmem::Finder` built once and reused, or `aho-corasick` for a multi-pattern set — hoisted out of the loop. Candidate sites to read first: `collect_service_call_sites` (8.1% self, 10.8% total) and the `line.contains(marker)` / `starts_with` scans around hilo-cli/src/commands/graph.rs:1036-1160. PREDICTION to falsify: hoisting the pattern should remove most of the `StrSearcher::new` self time; if it does not, the searcher is being built per-STRING and the loop structure is the thing to change, not the pattern.

FINDING C (whole-map clone, 10.9% self): `<BTreeMap<_,_,_> as Clone>::clone::clone_subtree` at 10.9% self is a full tree clone. Deep-copying an entire map is usually unnecessary ("PERF-003" in this repo made the same class of point about the debug binary); the usual fix is to borrow, or to wrap in `Rc`/`Arc` and clone the handle. Needs the call site located before any claim about which map it is.

FINDING D (I/O shape, 10.8% total): `std::fs::read_to_string::inner` is 10.8% of total with essentially all of it SELF — whole-file reads. Combined with `serde_json Value::deserialize` at 12.8% self this is the read+parse front half of the pipeline. Not automatically a defect (reading a file is supposed to cost), but it bounds what parse-level micro-optimisation can win: no amount of parser tuning removes the read.

FINDING E (duckdb worker threads, ~18% combined): `TaskScheduler::ExecuteForever` 8.0% and `ConcurrentQueue::DequeueFromProducer` 10.1% are DuckDB's own worker threads spinning/dequeuing. On a 16-core shared host with the manifest declaring threads: 4, this is worth measuring against a smaller `threads` value — if the work is not parallel enough to feed them, those threads are pure scheduling overhead. Cheap A/B: `hilo` with performance.duckdb.threads = 1 vs 4 under hyperfine.

FINDING F (allocation pressure): `_int_malloc` 6.1% + `String::clone` 5.3% + `BTreeMap::clone` 10.9% together point at copy-heavy data flow rather than an algorithmic problem.

MEASUREMENT HONESTY: n=420 samples is enough to rank a 36%-of-symbolized cluster but NOT enough to trust a 3-5% ordering; treat single-digit findings as leads, not conclusions. The hyperfine number is WARM-cached and must not be compared to a cold run. Criterion benches do not yet exist for reconcile/insert or stats(), so there is still no CI-visible regression guard for any of this — that remains the highest-value remaining item on this row.

PIPELINE ARTEFACTS: /tmp/prof_warm2.svg, /tmp/perf2.data, and the reusable scripts ~/.hermes/scripts/fgparse.py (custom SVG parsing, geometry + stacked formats) and ~/.hermes/scripts/prof-pipeline-proof2.sh (the whole chain in one command).

title: P2 — reconcile chunk size: the shipped RECONCILE_CHUNK_ROWS=2048 is NOT the fastest point; 512 is ~6% faster AND uses less peak memory (measured, Criterion)
detail: {"finding": "PERF-006's Criterion sweep (hilo-graph/benches/hotpath_bench.rs) measured the reconcile/insert path at 5000 edges across three chunk sizes.", "measurements_ms_mean_ci95": {"chunk_512": {"mean": 4183.19, "ci": [3986.42, 4457.26]}, "chunk_2048": {"mean": 4434.94, "ci": [4096.84, 4855.01], "note": "THE SHIPPED DEFAULT (RECONCILE_CHUNK_ROWS)"}, "chunk_8192": {"mean": 5067.16, "ci": [4885.84, 5271.87]}, "default_path": {"bench": "reconcile/5000-edges", "mean": 4909.17, "ci": [4443.51, 5514.31]}, "stats_5000_edges": {"mean_ms": 3.56, "ci": [3.49, 3.63]}}, "why_this_is_unsurprising": "GAP-092 introduced chunking as a MEMORY CEILING, not a throughput knob. Its default was chosen to bound peak RSS, and no measurement was ever taken of the total-time cost it traded. This row is that measurement finally being taken.", "why_it_matters": "512 wins on BOTH axes here — faster mean AND a smaller open transaction, so less peak memory. That means the shipped default is strictly dominated on this corpus, which is the rare case where a memory fix and a speed fix point the same direction.", "caveat_NOT_a_drop_in_change": "This is NOT authorised as a silent retune. Changing a shipped constant is a behaviour change: it alters peak memory on other corpora and may interact with GAP-095's spill watermark (spill_watermark vs chunk size). It needs its own gate and its own measurement at LARGER edge counts before the default moves.", "proposed_work": ["1. Re-run the sweep at the GAP-092 corpus scale (155K edges) — 5000 edges is small enough that fixed per-run overhead may dominate.", "2. Measure PEAK RSS (VmHWM) per chunk size, not just wall time — the whole point of the constant is the memory ceiling. A throughput-only comparison is insufficient.", "3. Check the interaction with the GAP-095 spill watermark: a chunk larger than the remaining headroom under memory_limit could defeat the ceiling it exists to enforce.", "4. Only then decide whether the default moves, and land it with the RSS numbers in the commit message."], "evidence": "PERF-006 row + commit 8c7d642 (hilo-graph/benches/hotpath_bench.rs); raw estimates under target/criterion/hotpath_reconcile-chunk-size_5000-edges/", "measurement_honesty": "Criterion's own `change:` percentages from that run are NOT usable — `base` was saved from the same run as `new`, so the deltas read +0.0%. Only the raw timings above are real."}
reasoning:
Derived from PERF-006's Criterion sweep, which was filed to create a CI-visible regression guard for the reconcile/insert and stats() paths. Building that guard immediately produced a number worth acting on.

The shipped default (2048) is not the minimum of the curve measured: 512 is ~6% faster with a smaller transaction. Since 2048 was chosen for MEMORY reasons and never timed, this is the expected shape of an untuned constant.

Filed rather than fixed because it is a shipped-constant change: it must be justified at the corpus scale it was originally chosen for (155K edges), with peak-RSS numbers, not extrapolated from a 5000-edge microbenchmark. A throughput win that quietly raises peak memory would be a regression against the very row (GAP-092/095) that introduced the constant.

detail: dogfood run 9 at HEAD 917a991 (v0.3.0, local release build). Session (scratch workspace, bare git remote prepared): (1) `hilo backend mount --type git --url file:///tmp/dogfood-warpfs-r9/remote.git --at code` -> stdout `mounted git file:///tmp/dogfood-warpfs-r9/remote.git at code (worktree code)`, EXIT=0 — but no `code/` directory is created, `.vfs/backends/` remains EMPTY (no mounts.yaml), no error of any kind. So the two paths disagree: the default/auto path lies about success and persists nothing; the explicit-tool path tells the truth and rejects. detail: {"measured": {"date": "2026-09-22", "corpus": "/tmp/bakeoff5/flask copied fresh (.vfs/graph/graph.db, .last_reconcile, graph.db.wal all deleted)"}, "A_mcp_fresh_default": {"secs": 0.0, "total_edges": 0, "edge_types": {}, "error": null}, "B_mcp_fresh_budget_60000ms": {"secs": 0.0, "total_edges": 0, "edge_types": {}, "meaning": "an explicit generous reconcile_budget_ms does NOT fix it -> the MCP path never attempts the reconcile at all"}, "C_cli_reconciled_then_mcp": {"secs": 0.03, "total_edges": 639, "edge_types": {"imports": 463, "tested_by": 176}, "meaning": "MCP answers correctly once a graph.db exists"}, "cli_control_same_corpus": {"total_edges_raw": 824, "distinct": 639}, "regression_test": {"wave6_binary_mcp_fresh": {"total_edges": 0}, "wave7_binary_mcp_fresh": {"total_edges": 0}, "wave6_binary_cli_fresh": "639 / 824", "wave7_binary_cli_fresh": "639 / 824", "conclusion": "PRE-EXISTING. Both binaries show it; it is not a GAP-094 regression."}, "why_severe": "An agent that wires hilo's MCP server into a fresh checkout receives an empty graph and cannot tell it apart from a genuinely dependency-free repo. This is the same silent-empty failure class GAP-059/GAP-062 closed on the CLI path; the MCP path still has it."}
reasoning:
Found while verifying GAP-094 in bake-off wave 7. I was specifically testing whether the wave-7 fix (reconcile_budget_ms) traded the old 207s blocking call for something worse, and probed the MCP path on a FRESH corpus for the first time — earlier waves only ever exercised MCP against an already-reconciled cache, which is why this went unnoticed.

OBSERVED: `hilo serve --mcp` + a JSON-RPC `vfs_graph_stats` on a corpus whose graph.db is absent returns {"edge_types":{}, "most_connected":null, "orphans":[], "total_edges":0, "total_files":0} in 0.0s. The one-shot CLI on an identical fresh copy returns 639 distinct / 824 raw edges. Same binary, same corpus, same moment — only the entry point differs.

NOT A GAP-094 REGRESSION — checked deliberately with the wave-6 binary: it returns 0 too, and its CLI returns 639/824. So this is a long-standing MCP-path defect, not something the memory work introduced. Filing it now because the bake-off is the first time it has been exercised.

NOT THE BUDGET either: setting performance.duckdb.reconcile_budget_ms=60000 on the fresh corpus changes nothing (still 0 edges, still 0.0s). The MCP path does not call reconcile_edges_from_jsonl at all — it opens the graph and reads whatever is there. The fix is therefore to make the MCP entry point run the same reconcile the CLI runs (bounded by reconcile_budget_ms), and — critically — to make an un-reconciled or partially-reconciled read VISIBLE rather than silently empty.

ACCEPTANCE: fresh corpus + MCP vfs_graph_stats must return the same edge totals the CLI returns (639/824 on flask), or must fail loudly naming the reason. A test must pin this: delete graph.db, call over MCP, assert the answer matches the CLI.
